newsitem.title: USA: Simpson prosecutor Clark to host TV show.
newsitem.headline: Simpson prosecutor Clark to host TV show.

text.p: Marcia Clark, the lead prosecutor in O.J. Simpson's criminal murder trial, is quitting the Los Angeles District Attorney's office to host a new TV show about women in law enforcement.
Clark, who spent 14 years at the D.A.'s office, and is currently writing a book about the Simpson trial, will host a half-hour show called "Lady Law", the producers said on Thursday.
They described the show as "reality-based" -- like the successful "Cops" series -- and said it would focus on "the extraordinary women in the field of law enforcement."
"Lady Law" is currently in production and will be introduced at next week's NATPE '97 trade show, said the executive producers, who hoped to sell it in syndication.
Clark will host the daily show and contribute voice-overs, although she will not conduct interviews, said a spokeswoman.

"From cops on the street, corrections officers, parole officers, Border Patrol, DEA, FBI, Secret Service and military personnel to judges and prosecutors, the series will be a tribute to dedicated women in all fields of law enforcement," the producers said in a statement.

"I'm honoured to have been chosen to help present the stories of the admirable and distinguished women who have chosen to accept the challenges of a demanding yet fulfilling career in law enforcement," Clark said.

She has been on leave from the D.A.'s office since the Simpson trial ended in October 1995 in personal failure for her when the former football star was acquitted of murdering his ex-wife and her friend.
